body: The testdata def file should move out of the regressions directory as well and be more descriptively named.

Rather than having custom environment variables for testing, I asked Cedric and he suggested adding hidden command line option(s) in cmd/internal/build.go, with associated environment variables.  That gives the most consistency in dealing with environment variables, and code in cmd/internal/cli can just refer to the flag's variable name instead of reading an environment variable at all.

Cedric suggested a single hidden option called `--fakeroot-mode` but I'm thinking more generically.  I suggest more than one option:
1. A non-hidden `--userns` option, to match what is used with action flags, except there can't be a shorthand `-u` because it is already taken.  Then `APPTAINER_USERNS=1` can be set for modes 1b, 2, and 3.
2. A hidden `--ignore-subuid` option to ignore `/etc/subuid` entries.  Then `APPTAINER_IGNORE_SUBUID=1` can be set for modes 2 through 4.
3. A hidden `--ignore-fakeroot-command` option to ignore the fakeroot command.  Then `APPTAINER_IGNORE_FAKEROOT_COMMAND=1` can be set for mode 3.
4. A hidden `--ignore-userns` option to ignore user namespaces.  Then `APPTAINER_IGNORE_USERNS=1` can be set for mode 4.

Since the `--fakeroot` option is also supported in the same way for action commands, I think it would be good at the same time to add the hidden options 2 through 4 above also to the action flags.

The ignoreUserns and userns options aren't relevant here.  The relevant one is ignoreSubuid.  The if should be
```
    if uid != 0 && (!fakeroot.IsUIDMapped(uid) || buildArgs.ignoreSubuid) {

Do most of the tests on sif instead of sandbox.  They should work except in mode 2 openssh will fail but some simpler package will succeed, and mode 4 does require a sandbox.  Actually I tested it with an alpine container and that succeeds too so switch to a centos 7 container like you have with build and use yum -y install.  Then mode 2 can install epel-release successfully.
typo `namesapce` -> `namespace`
Delete this line (and modify preceding comment); useSuid is already set to false when the `--userns` flag is given, and `--ignore-subuid` is not relevant to this.

Unfortunately I found that the suid mode (for modes 1a and 4) with `--writable-tmpfs` defaults to only 16M which is not enough for installing openssh on centos7.   You can increase the amount for the test.  First do
```
sudo singularity config global -g "sessiondir max size"
```
to get the current size (defaults to 16) and do
```
sudo singularity config global -s "sessiondir max size" 1024
```
to set it high enough, and then at the end restore the original value.

This will also affect any other tests running in parallel but it shouldn't cause any harm.

body:
It's good that you found a way to do that, but I think we can do better.

If I understand correctly the way it works, the GOROOT setting above is not getting interpreted by the make command which I presume the debian packaging invokes on this.  It is just getting passed as a raw string to the shell, after replacing the two dollar signs with one.

So, you should be able to put here
```
GOCACHE = $${TMPDIR:/tmp}/appdebgo/cache
```
and then add `GOCACHE=$(GOCACHE)` to the following command line directly after the setting of PATH. That will export the variable only to that command.

Another thing to note is that each line of shell commands is separately sent to the shell, so you can't set a variable on one line and expect it to be set in the next line. That's why there are sometimes many lines separated by a semicolon and backslash, which makes them all be one shell invocation.

body:
That's probably true, but using fusermount to do the fuse mount (in addition to the fact that it can't be done in a root-restricted environment such as inside an apptainer container) means that cleanup can be a mess. For example, if it is killed with `kill -9` (or maybe even a `^C`, you might want to try that) then there will be a leftover mount that's connected to nothing which will get `Transport endpoint is not connected` errors.
 
I think it should be possible to do the original mount in a new root-mapped unprivileged user+mount namespace.  We probably could even make it a pid namespace as well which will make sure that the FUSE process exits when the namespace is shut down.   The [`fakeroot.UnshareRootMapped()`](https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/blob/release-1.1/internal/pkg/fakeroot/fakefake.go#L29) function may be close to what you need, and I am about to modify it to add a mount namespace so it can bind mount the home directory.  You would need to make sure the same namespace stays in place for the duration of the command, not just execute a subcommand in it, so the mountpoint stays available to the rest of the code.  The way that function is designed to be used is to pass `os.Args` to it like [here](https://github.com/apptainer/apptainer/blob/main/internal/pkg/runtime/launch/launcher_linux.go#L123) so it re-executes the whole program from scratch.  The next time through it detects that things are already set up and then skips the re-exec.

Instead, signals should be caught and the image driver stop() function called (or its equivalent if not using the image driver), as is done for action commands. body: It bothers me quite a bit that this function has significant overlap with the image driver and yet is implemented differently.  I think it might come back to bite us later.  It was things like this that made me hope you could use the image driver directly from the build code.

Rather than hardcoding the number of times through the loop, it's better to use the approach in the image driver of setting a maxTime and keeping track of the totTime.  That way the length of time between each check and the maximum can both be independently controlled.

I just realized that checking for a suid install or `--userns` here is a bug.  A suid install is not relevant to this type of build.  I verified this by temporarily renaming fusermount and fusermount3, then it failed with 
```
ERROR:   Gocryptfs mount has error, err: <nil>
FATAL:   While performing build: while employing gocryptfs to create image, err: could not start gocryptfs command, error occurs
```
(which also indicates that the gocryptfs execution code is not correctly catching errors).

So this check should just be for `if buildArgs.encrypt` because it is already under a check for not running as root, which means it is running unprivileged.

Then unfortunately the parameter to fakerootExec also needs to be more complicated, so the message inside if UnshareRootMapped fails can distinguish regarding whether or not it has to check`!useSuid`.  I think it's easiest to make it two bools; instead of `required bool` make it `isDeffile bool, unprivEncrypt bool` and restore the previous check and message for `!useSuid && isDeffile` and add an additional check
```
if unprivEncrypt {
        sylog.Fatalf("Building with encryption unprivileged requires unprivileged user namespaces")
}
```

we are acutally using goarch value here, but to map it to docker image archs, we need a map.
yes, it's mapping the docker image <-> golang arch

docker hub actually returns the manifest based on the uri (docker://image:tag or docker://amd64/image:tag)
if you test with the following commands:
`apptainer --debug pull --arch amd64 test.sif docker://alpine:latest`

manifest digest
```
DEBUG   [U=1000,P=853141]  getRefDigest()                GetManifest digest for docker://alpine:latest is 124c7d2707904eea7431fffe91522a01e5a861a624ee31d03372cc1d138a3126
```

and
`apptainer --debug pull test.sif docker://amd64/alpine:latest`

manifest digest
```
DEBUG   [U=1000,P=853900]  getDockerRefDigest()          docker.GetDigest digest for docker://amd64/alpine:latest is b6ca290b6b4cdcca5b3db3ffa338ee0285c11744b4a6abaa9627746ee3291d8d
```

The root cause is that `docker://alpine:latest` will return a combined manifest containing multi-archs, while `docker://amd64/alpine:latest` will only return a manifest containing single-(reqiuired) arch. 
Though they are actually downloading the same image, the cache will fail in this case. So one way is to convert the `docker://amd64/alpine:latest` to `docker://alpine:latest` to retrieve the unified digest.
I think you can remove `pullArch` here and use `ArchitectureChoice` in `types.SystemContext`
`getRefDigest` should follow the new hash computation logic (digest+arch), currently it looks like only pull will use this new digest, build will keep using old digest leading to cache miss

This is shown with an apptainer suid install:
```
$ apptainer exec -f --no-home --writable --ignore-userns --ignore-subuid ubuntu-22.04.sandbox sh -c 'cat /proc/$$/uid_map'
INFO:    User not listed in /etc/subuid, trying root-mapped namespace

WARNING: Skipping mount /etc/localtime [binds]: /etc/localtime doesn't exist in container
         0       3382          1
         1     100000      65536
```

This is I think the key change that went into the original PR, but it turns out to be redundant for apptainer because `namespaces.IsUnprivileged()` already covers all the cases that `namespaces.IsInsideUserNamespace(os.Getpid())` covers.  In fact, I don't think apptainer has the problem at all that was being addressed by that PR, that of running under `unshare -r` and `unshare -c`.  They both work for me (the latter on EL9 because it doesn't exist on EL8).

I'm not sure it's a good idea to change all these messages to debug level.

The nested apptainer is invoked with `--pwd /` so I'm pretty sure it's only the second case that we care about.  How about it stays as a warning if `cwdHost == ""` but doesn't print anything if `cwdHost == "/"`.
Are you sure this is actually relevant?  I'd rather keep it as a warning.

This might be overkill since normally the command line message level setting is passed on to the nested apptainer.  I guess if someone set the environment variable instead of the command line, this would help.  But I'm worried about extraneous INFO messages in the default condition of no messagelevel settings or command line options.  For example what happens if you don't have subuid mapping set up, are there any INFO messages shown again regarding fakeroot?
